doc.title: Jane Bunnett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 25, 2024

chapter: Playing, recording and making a living
title: Dancing, playing for dancers and Barry Harris on bebop
summary: She loves to dance, likes playing for dancers, and recalls Barry Harris on bebop ending dancing and Fred Taylor's tap shows.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Let me ask you about dance. This is an odd question. Do you and Larry dance?
I love to dance. Larry not so much.
Okay. I saw one video of you playing in — I don’t know if it was a club or whatever. And people were dancing.
And I love playing for dancers. I think it effects the band positively if things are in sync.

It’s really true. I like playing for dancers too. Yeah, I really do. Yeah a lot of the time at our shows people will get up and dance, it depends on the particular city. Some cities are more — have a tendency to more kind of hippies and those folks come out. But yeah, I mean I remember Barry Harris and I think a lot of other musicians of that era, the late Barry Harris saying that you know when people stop dancing, you know when the bebop started to really develop people stopped dancing and that was a really unfortunate aspect for the music because it sort of then kind of made a distance between the musicians and the audience members. And that’s why it’s great, I don’t know if you ever knew Fred Taylor, a wonderful man who booked Sculler’s in Cambridge, Massachusetts but he was one of the first guys to put on shows with tap dancers and some of the drummers. I’m sorry I can’t remember — I want to say Jo Jones but I don’t know if it was Jo Jones. I think it might have been Jo Jones. And Jimmy Slyde and some of the great dancers, tap dancers. That was really, what do you call it — a collaboration, a beautiful collaboration.
